items.q: Construct a line segment 6 cm long and find its midpoint. Where is the midpoint?
hints: The midpoint splits the segment into two equal parts — divide the total length by 2.
3 cm from each end

items.q: What angle should a constructed perpendicular make with the line?
hints: Recall the definition of 'perpendicular'.
Perpendicular lines always meet at a right angle.

items.q: A construction uses arcs from both endpoints of a segment. What line do the arc intersections help construct?
hints: Think about what is equidistant from both endpoints where the arcs cross.
The two arc intersection points are equidistant from both ends, so the line through them is the perpendicular bisector.
Perpendicular bisector

items.q: What does SSS mean when constructing a triangle?
hints: SSS names the three pieces of information you're given to construct the triangle.
You are given all three side lengths of the triangle.
Side-side-side

items.q: In a valid construction, should measurements be guessed freehand?
hints: Think about what makes a construction accurate and valid.
A construction must use compass and straightedge measurements precisely, not estimates.
No

items.q: What tool is used to draw the arc in a construction?
hints: Recall which tool draws curved, equal-radius marks.
A compass is set to a fixed radius and used to draw arcs.
Compass

items.q: Name two tools needed for geometric constructions.
hints: Recall the two standard tools used for constructions (no protractor allowed).
Constructions use a compass for arcs and a straight ruler for lines.
Compass and ruler

items.q: Why should the compass width stay fixed when drawing equal arcs?
hints: Think about what changing the compass width would do to the arcs.
If the compass width changed, the arcs would no longer be the same distance from the centre.
To keep the radius equal

items.q: What should be drawn lightly first in a construction?
hints: Think about which marks are working lines rather than the final answer.
The arcs are guide marks, so they should be light until the final lines are confirmed.
Construction arcs

items.q: What does a ruler without markings help preserve in constructions?
hints: Think about what a ruler is used for in a construction, aside from measuring.
A plain edge is used purely to draw a straight line accurately between two points.
Accuracy of straight lines

items.q: Should construction lines usually be erased before checking?
hints: Think about what a teacher or examiner needs to see to check your method.
The construction arcs and lines should be left visible as evidence of the method used.
No

items.q: What is the main purpose of a compass in constructions?
hints: Recall what a fixed compass radius lets you mark out repeatedly.
A compass lets you draw arcs that are all the same fixed distance from a point.
Drawing equal distances or arcs

items.q: If an angle is 70°, what is each half after bisecting?
hints: Bisecting an angle splits it exactly in half.

items.q: If an angle is 118°, what is each half after bisecting?
hints: Bisecting an angle splits it exactly in half.

items.q: What do points on an angle bisector have equal distance from?
hints: Recall the defining property of every point on an angle bisector.
Every point on the bisector is the same perpendicular distance from each of the two arms.
Both arms of the angle

items.q: If an angle is 96°, what is each half after bisecting?
hints: Bisecting an angle splits it exactly in half.

items.q: A bisected angle gives two equal angles of 27°. What was the original angle?
hints: Reverse the bisection by doubling one half.

items.q: What tool is essential for constructing an angle bisector?
hints: Recall which tool draws the equal-radius arcs needed for this construction.
A compass is used to mark equal-radius arcs from the vertex and from those points.
Compass

items.q: What angle does a perpendicular bisector make with the segment?
hints: Recall the definition of 'perpendicular'.
Perpendicular lines always meet at a right angle.

items.q: What does a perpendicular bisector do to a line segment?
items.a: Cuts it into two equal parts
hints: Recall what 'bisector' means for a line segment.
A bisector divides the segment into two equal halves.
Cuts it into two equal parts

items.q: What is the locus of points equidistant from A and B?
hints: Think about which line contains every point that is the same distance from both A and B.
That set of equidistant points forms the perpendicular bisector of AB.
Perpendicular bisector

items.q: A segment is 14 cm long. Where is the midpoint on its perpendicular bisector?
hints: The perpendicular bisector crosses the segment at its midpoint — divide the total length by 2.
7 cm from each end

items.q: True or false: a perpendicular bisector passes through the midpoint.
hints: Recall what 'bisector' means for the segment it crosses.
By definition, a bisector cuts a segment exactly at its midpoint.
True

items.q: What pair of arcs are used to construct a perpendicular bisector?
hints: Think about which two arcs, when drawn from the endpoints, cross at points equidistant from both ends.
Arcs of the same radius drawn from each endpoint intersect at two points equidistant from both.
Equal-radius arcs from each endpoint

items.q: If one side of an equilateral triangle is 8 cm, what are the other sides?
hints: Recall what 'equilateral' means for the sides of a triangle.
All three sides of an equilateral triangle are equal in length.
8 cm each

items.q: What is each interior angle of an equilateral triangle?
hints: The three equal angles must add up to 180°, like any triangle.

items.q: When constructing an equilateral triangle, what compass radius is used from each endpoint?
hints: Think about what distance the compass needs to mark out for all three sides to end up equal.
Setting the compass to the side length and drawing arcs from both endpoints locates the third vertex at that same distance from each.
The side length

items.q: If an equilateral triangle has side 5 cm, what is its perimeter?
hints: Add up all three equal sides.

items.q: True or false: all angles in an equilateral triangle are equal.
hints: Recall the defining property of an equilateral triangle's angles.
Equal sides in a triangle always produce equal opposite angles — so all three angles are equal.
True

items.q: What shape is formed when three sides are all equal?
hints: Recall the name for a triangle whose three sides all match.
A triangle with all three sides equal in length is called equilateral.
Equilateral triangle
